Custom Ford Raptor R Packs 1,000 Horsepower on Deep Concave Silver Polished 22s and 37-Inch Tires
7 photos
Photo: vossen / Instagram
It's been a rather long minute since we last discussed something shown by custom forged and hybrid forged wheel specialist Vossen , and it's time to make amends to the Miami, Florida-based company. With this 1,000-horsepower Ford F-150 Raptor R, of course.
The Ford F-Series was born as a series of light-duty trucks succeeding the 1941-1948 Ford pickup truck model back in 1948, taking its place between the current mid-size Ford Ranger and the heavy-duty truck series, and including the Super Duty models since 1999. Throughout its history, the most famous monikers have been the F-100 and later the F-150, introduced in 1975.
Widely regarded as one of the best full-size pickup trucks, the F-Series has also brought an important series of records to the Blue Oval – it’s been the top-selling pickup truck line in the United States since 1977 and also the best-selling nameplate, overall, since 1981. That’s almost half a century of continued dominance, which is a massive achievement.
As such, it’s no surprise that the fourteenth generation remains extremely popular, even after setbacks like the failed F-150 Lightning all-electric model. Right now, after the 2024 refresh, the 2027 model year of the Ford F-150 includes the XL model from $38,110, along with the STX, XLT, Lariat, King Ranch, Platinum, Tremor, and Raptor versions, with MSRPs surging to $75,820. Actually, if you want the Ford F-150 Raptor R instead of the regular model with the 450 hp and 510 lb-ft of torque 3.5-liter high-output EcoBoost V6, you will have to pay more.
The 5.2-liter supercharged Predator V8 engine shared with the 2027 Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC and the Mustang GT supercar is a package costing another $37,045 on top of the Raptor’s MSRP. Of course, the most powerful engine offered on the F-150 Raptor truck is tuned specifically for this application and develops ‘just’ 720 horsepower instead of 795 or 815 hp like on the Mustangs.
But some folks don’t care that it’s now again below the 2027 Ram 1500 TRX SRT , which has returned with the Hemi V8 under the hood and the 6.2-liter supercharged engine packing 777 horsepower. Instead, all they care about are the looks and capabilities. Most likely that’s the case here, too, as Vossen decided to share the beauty shots of a pristine example dressed in Oxford White and rocking a series of custom enhancements and modifications.
Those include the color-matched front and rear bumpers plus the hood and fender flares, the massive set of LED lights embedded into the front bumper, as well as the matching white Raptor branding. But, of course, the most enticing feature is the wheel and tire package, which consists of 22 by 12-inch Vossen HFX-4 six-lug alloy wheels finished in Silver Polished and shod in massive Toyo Tires 37-inch by 12.5 R22s!
The Vossen HFX-4 hybrid forged alloy wheels have a starting price of $649 each and come with 19 through 24-inch diameters or 9.5 through 13-inch widths, but that’s for the five-lug version. The six-lug variant fitted on the Oxford White Ford F-150 Raptor R are actually cheaper, starting from $525 and are a go for 17-24-inch diameters and 8.5-12-inch widths. This version seen here is also deeply concave, adding to the drama of the build.
Alas, maybe a 1,000-horsepower Ford F-150 Raptor R like this one, as per the description, isn’t your cup of tea, even though now it can make short work of that 777-hp Ram 1500 TRX SRT. No worries, because Vossen also has other stuff to brag about.
If you want a contemporary mid-engine supercar like the 907-hp plug-in hybrid V8-powered Lamborghini Temerario, then you’re in luck because they just showcased the first Viola Parsifae Lambo Temerario featuring the 7Design Aria Carbon kit, and the setup was also tucked on Vossen Forged GEN-22 wheels finished in Dark Smoke.
It was one of the many Vossen-equipped vehicles on the floor at the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, by the way. If you would rather go with a boxy luxury SUV, they also showed us the first Mercedes-AMG G 63 featuring the full Urban Automotive Widetrack kit and tucked on Urban x Vossen UV-9 alloy wheels that pose a shiny contrast against the Inozetek Super Gloss Navy Blue wrap for the body.
Alternatively, we can ogle all day long at an Aston Martin Valhalla on the new Vossen G2-10 wheels featuring the L2 Lip configuration or a Verde British Racing Ferrari Purosangue on Vossen S21-02 three-piece alloy wheels in Polished Gloss Clear and lowered on a set of Novitec suspension components. So, which one is your favorite and why?
